milestones.title: Foundations and the differential oracle
milestones.goal: The workspace builds to wasm and to native, and the oracle renders the corpus through cornerstone3D before any port code exists.

milestones.title: DICOM ingest and the pixel pipeline
milestones.goal: A frame parses, decodes and passes the hand-computed LUT fixtures of HLD section 18.3.

milestones.title: Cache and the render core
milestones.goal: One budgeted cache, one wgpu device, the LUT chain running as a shader stage on both capability tiers.

milestones.title: Public API, the boundary, and the stack viewport
milestones.goal: The three-channel boundary is real and a stack viewport diffs clean against cornerstone3D. This is the Phase 1 credibility gate.

milestones.title: Volume, MPR and 3D rendering
milestones.goal: Volumes assemble progressively, reslice obliquely and ray-cast on both tiers.

milestones.title: Segmentation rendering
milestones.goal: All three representations render: labelmap, contour, surface.

milestones.title: Tool framework and geometry
milestones.goal: Interaction state in TypeScript, hit-testing and measurement mathematics in Rust.

milestones.title: Annotation tools
milestones.goal: The 26 annotation classes and the ROI statistics engine.

milestones.title: Segmentation tools
milestones.goal: The 12 segmentation classes.

milestones.title: Manipulation and utility tools
milestones.goal: The 25 manipulation and utility classes.

milestones.title: Annotation state and DICOM interop
milestones.goal: SR is the native annotation type, and SEG, RTSTRUCT and TID 1500 round trip.

milestones.title: Migration and rollout
milestones.goal: Both libraries coexist, viewport by viewport, with shadow mode before each cutover.

milestones.title: Performance, hardening and release
milestones.goal: Binary size and cold start inside budget, the browser matrix certified, semver and provenance policy in force.

milestones.title: Series open in the core and the viewer
milestones.goal: The series-open gaps that Phase 1 left in the core, then the example viewer calling that core.

milestones.title: Local folder viewer
milestones.goal: The local folder viewer opens a synthetic study or a folder, and the page shows the image tools, the marks, and how to call the library.

milestones.title: Out-of-core volume streaming
milestones.goal: Bounded GPU residency on unbounded data. The first of the three checkable claims in HLD C.7.

milestones.title: The WebGPU compute subsystem
milestones.goal: Kernels sharing the renderer's device, every tier-A kernel carrying a declared fallback.

milestones.title: Prompted segmentation and standards-native annotations
milestones.goal: SAM2-class prompting against GPU-resident tensors, and GSPS write with coded concepts.

milestones.title: Multi-monitor, attestation and live sessions
milestones.goal: Real multi-monitor, a published divergence bound, and a CRDT over state that is already a serialisable struct.

milestones.title: Whole-slide imaging and the unified scene graph
milestones.goal: Radiology and pathology in one scene graph, sharing one annotation coordinate model.

stories.story: JPEG-LS decoded per ITU-T T.87: the vendored ritk-codecs scan decoder raises the run index only for a full run segment, a scan that runs out of data or leaves unread bytes before EOI is refused, an LSE preset this decoder does not apply is refused by name, default thresholds clamp as C.2.4.1.1.1 gives them, with CharLS-encoded trigger fixtures and banded corpus rows under .80 and .81
stories.notes: Decided by the operator on 2026-11-07: a monochrome JPEG-LS frame with a long flat run ending a line decodes to wrong pixels with no error. The vendored run-mode loop raises RUNindex on a partial end-of-line segment, and the scan decoder never refuses a desynchronised or truncated scan. This story patches the vendored decoder, lands before F-239's codec part, and F-239's ritk-codecs patch merges onto it. E4.13 rather than E4.9, which F-145's recorded defect declares.

Tier C, software-adapter detection, and the feature-availability contract
stories.notes: Deviation D-07, and spike answer docs/spikes/A7-tier-c.md. HLD section 7 declares TWO tiers and both are GPU, so a machine with neither WebGPU nor WebGL2 renders nothing. Adds Tier::Cpu, and generalises the section 31 kernel rule to every tier-gated feature: a feature that cannot run on the resolved tier reports UNAVAILABLE and never silently produces a different answer. SCOPE ADDED BY A7.1: tier resolution must distinguish a HARDWARE adapter from a SOFTWARE one. On a host with no GPU a software rasteriser presents a conforming WebGL2 context, so Caps as specified resolves tier B and runs GPU paths on a rasteriser that is slower than our own CPU path and burns more CPU, which on a shared host is the resource that decides session density. Detect by renderer string, adapter type AND a startup micro-benchmark, and trust the benchmark: a renderer string is a claim and increasingly masked, a measured fill rate is a fact. Always allow an operator override.

stories.story: Three-layer GPU-less render testing: lavapipe in CI and Chrome with SwiftShader nightly
stories.notes: Spike answer A7.2. Layer 1, tier C raster, needs NO adapter and is a plain cargo test on every PR, which is why the bulk of tier C correctness is free in CI. This story builds layers 2 and 3. Layer 2 is lavapipe via wgpu force_fallback_adapter on ubuntu-latest, catching pipeline construction, bind-group layouts, WGSL compilation and the tier-B shader variants at no GPU cost. Layer 3 is headless Chrome with SwiftShader, nightly or manual, and it is the only layer that says anything about what a GPU-less session actually does. DO NOT describe layer 2 as a simulator of a real GPU-less session: lavapipe is Vulkan through wgpu, a GPU-less browser session is SwiftShader through Chrome WebGL2. NO layer is an oracle, the reference is cornerstone3D per section 11. ACCEPTANCE: prove lavapipe actually resolves as a fallback adapter under the pinned wgpu version on ubuntu-latest. If it does not, layer 2 drops and layers 1 and 3 stand.

stories.story: CPU raster for the stack viewport, progressive refinement, and the tier A against C bound
stories.notes: HLD section 18 requires the LUT chain to exist once in ocelli-pixel with the shader reading its parameters, so the CPU path reuses that implementation and does not use the shader. One arithmetic implementation, three presentation paths. Inner loops use wasm SIMD128, and the no-SIMD runtime is measured separately as the worst case. A7.3b, PROGRESSIVE REFINEMENT: reduced resolution during a window/level drag or scroll, full resolution on settle. Same idiom as sections 8 and 30. It cuts CPU when the budget is under pressure AND cuts full-frame changes for a remoted session's display encoder, which is the second cost and the easy one to forget. Two constraints follow: the SETTLED frame is what the divergence bound is measured on, an interaction frame is explicitly not claimed to match tier A, and the user must be able to tell settled from refining because a radiologist must never measure from a frame that is still refining. A7.3, CPU BUDGET: measure the incumbent viewer on a representative GPU-less session, budget is no worse than its interactive AND idle cost, then record and gate on regression using the same mechanism as ci/wasm-size-budget.json. Report interactive and idle separately. Idle must be indistinguishable from zero because it multiplies by every open session on the host. A7.1b, DIVERGENCE: the estate is mixed, so decision D14's published bound must cover tier A against tier C. The oracle diffs the two over the corpus.

stories.story: CPU MPR and oblique reslicing, with SIMD inner loops
stories.notes: REQUIRED, not optional, and split from the volume decision by spike answer A7.1b. GPU passthrough is not assumed, so a user on a GPU-less session has no other route to a reformat at all: without this, that whole deployment class gets stack viewing and nothing else. Reslicing is a resampling problem and is CPU-tractable for a single plane at interactive rates. Inner loops use wasm SIMD128, and the no-SIMD runtime is measured separately because that combination is the genuine worst case. Judged on CPU cost per session as well as latency, because on a shared host density is sessions per host.

stories.story: The CPU volume-rendering decision, and honest unavailability
stories.notes: A DECISION story, not an implementation one. Interactive volume ray-casting on CPU is very likely not achievable inside a GPU-less session's CPU budget, and the expected outcome is that VOLUME_3D reports UNAVAILABLE on tier C. That is a legitimate outcome and it is the whole point of the feature-availability contract in F-X001. What it must NOT do is the third thing: a slow CPU path that quietly produces a different image from the GPU one. Whichever way it goes, the shell must say so to the user in terms a radiologist can act on, because a 3D tab that is simply absent is a support call and a 3D tab that renders wrongly is a patient-safety issue.

stories.story: Answer Appendix A gates A1 (HTJ2K) and A2 (JPEG-LS) against our own decoders
stories.notes: F-010 established that cornerstone3D 5.8.2 RENDERS all three HTJ2K rows and both JPEG-LS rows, and its own review pass 6 caught the harness claiming that this answers A1 and A2. It does not. A1 asks whether HTJ2K decodes bit-exact through openjp2 UNDER wasm32, diffed against OpenJPH. A2 asks what Ocelli's JPEG-LS answer is at all, between a CharLS bridge, a self-compiled CharLS and a young pure-Rust crate. Both are questions about OUR decoder choices, and the reference implementation's ability to display those rows bears on neither. HLD Appendix A says each gate can end or reshape the programme and belongs in the first six weeks, and A2 says decide before anything else. The inputs already exist: the corpus carries a row per transfer syntax, OpenJPH 0.31.0 and DCMTK are installed, and the dicom-tooling skill documents dcmdjpls as the independent JPEG-LS decode. Deliver a written answer per gate in docs/spikes/, not a passing test.

stories.story: Oracle volume and MPR reference renders, so the spacing rows are asked something

stories.story: One parity-target version string, and a licence in the published wasm package
stories.notes: Deviation D-11 pins cornerstone3D at 5.8.2 because Appendix B's v5.8.9 does not exist on npm. F-010 corrected CLAUDE.md. The string v5.8.9 survives in .claude/commands/parity.md, docs/RELEASE.md, scripts/gen_sprint_plan.py and the SPRINT_PLAN.md it generates, plus the generated adapter under .agents/skills/. A parity target stated three ways is worse than one stated wrongly, because a reader cannot tell which is current. Fix the generator rather than its output. Carried with it, from F-002: wasm-pack warns that crates/ocelli-wasm carries no LICENSE file, so the generated package would publish with a licence field and no licence text, which is the same defect F-003 fixed for the npm packages.

stories.story: A standing test for every repository guard, not a mutation run once at authoring time
stories.notes: The root cause F-010's review loop identified at pass 13, quoted: round 12 mutated its guards in the same command that added them, which proves the guard fired once and leaves nothing watching it afterwards. That shape recurred across passes 9 to 13 and is not confined to the oracle. The repository now runs twenty-one floor gates, and most are guards whose red path has been observed exactly once, by hand, by the story that wrote them. docs/runbooks/guard-verification.md records the procedure and nothing executes it. Give every guard a standing test that fails when the guard stops guarding, so that a guard silently weakened by a refactor is caught by CI rather than by the next person who happens to try it.

stories.story: CI floor equivalence, and the identical --sprint and --all gate profiles
stories.notes: Two limits this sprint recorded rather than fixed. First, scripts/ci_floor_check.py asserts that CI INVOKES every floor gate and not that the invocation is EQUIVALENT: a workflow step running cargo clippy without -D warnings satisfies it today. Its own docstring says so. Closing it means either CI calling bin/ocelli.sh gate --floor per area, which collapses the job matrix that gives CI its useful per-area failure names, or comparing the command strings, and that is a design decision rather than a patch. Second, F-010 removed the S01 pre-oracle exception, which was the only thing distinguishing gates_cmd's --sprint arm from its --all arm, and the two are now character-identical. Either collapse them or give --sprint a distinction worth having.

stories.story: Cross-machine reference determinism, and what the oracle claims about it
stories.notes: F-010 claims determinism it can support: identical digests across two runs on one machine and one browser build, with SwiftShader forced so the reference does not depend on a GPU. It does not claim cross-machine reproducibility, and decision D14 is why the stronger claim is not made. That leaves an untested assumption at the point the oracle becomes shared: a second developer, or CI on manual dispatch, may produce different reference digests for reasons nobody has measured, and the failure would present as a port defect in F-011 rather than as an environment difference. Measure it on a second machine and a second Chromium build, publish the observed bound, and make run.json carry whatever identifies the difference.

stories.story: The reference's own SIGMOID width divergence, and what D14's bound says about it
stories.notes: F-010 found a defect in the REFERENCE, not in this project. cornerstone3D 5.8.2's toLowHighRange applies LINEAR's (w - 1) / 2 to SIGMOID, and PS3.3 C.11.2.1.3.1 gives SIGMOID its own width constraint which is not LINEAR's. F-010's own minimumWidth is PS3.3-correct and therefore disagrees with the reference. It is unreachable today because all 85 windowed corpus rows resolve LINEAR, and the first SIGMOID row added to the corpus meets it. This matters more than its size suggests: decision D14 commits to publishing a MEASURED divergence against cornerstone3D, and here the oracle would be measuring our correct arithmetic against the reference's incorrect arithmetic and reporting it as our divergence. Decide and record which side the bound is stated against, add a SIGMOID corpus row so the case is exercised rather than reasoned about, and state the answer in docs/lld/oracle.md where the divergence is already recorded.

stories.story: Price the HTJ2K decoder route after gate A1 failed
stories.notes: Appendix A gate A1 is answered Fail by F-X006 and its consequence is in force, so C codec builds are maintained regardless and one of the four arguments for the rewrite weakens. Measured: openjp2 0.6.1 does not link for wasm32-unknown-unknown, because src/malloc.rs declares malloc, calloc, realloc and free inside extern C with no cfg guard and the lib target declares a cdylib, so cargo links one even as a dependency and the link reports 432 undefined symbols. Forced to link with an allocator shim it then refuses every codestream by trapping, and two JPEG 2000 Part 1 rows decoded through the same build as a control show the failure is not confined to the HTJ2K path. A separate latent defect was found in the same crate, a null pointer reaching its deallocator, which is undefined behaviour on every target and not only on wasm. F-X006 priced three routes and chose none, because the design round said the fallback is priced in its own story. F3, the pure-Rust openjph-core 0.1.0 under BSD-2-Clause, is the one to measure FIRST, because it is the only route that is one implementation on every target, which is the same property that decided A2. Its risk is stated: first and only publish 2026-03-20 and crates.io reports no repository URL, so docs/SOURCE-POLICY.md question 1 cannot be answered from a repository. F1 is an upstream fix to openjp2, small but on a third-party release cycle. F2 is the JS-side codec-openjph the reference itself uses, which leaves the native desktop and server targets with no HTJ2K decoder at all and so has the hole D2's payoff exists to avoid. Until this answers, HTJ2K reports unavailable, which is section 31's rule and deviation D-07's rule generalised. A deviation against HLD section 15.2's sentence that openjp2 is what you select on wasm is owed by whichever story activates a codec feature.

stories.story: Close the two guard holes F-X009 declared, and watch the refusals its census leaves to nothing
stories.notes: TWO PARTS, and the second was added by the S03 review's third pass because it had been parked on a story that does not cover it. PART ONE, the declared holes. F-X009 gave every repository refusal a standing probe and declared four existing guards defective rather than fixing them, which was the right call for a story whose job was the census. TWO were closed during the S03 sprint review's second pass and their declarations removed in the same change, which is the two-directional ratchet working: a declared defect whose probe starts passing fails the gate until the declaration goes. G-01 is closed, ci_floor_check.py no longer does a substring test at all, and closing it turned up a live instance nobody had suspected, since corpus-tests was passing only on a comment in ci.yml while CI actually ran the script through a different interpreter. G-03 is closed, pin_and_size_check.py now parses Cargo.toml with tomllib and reads the version key rather than the first quoted string, which removes a demonstrated bypass of a CLAUDE.md hard rule. TWO REMAIN. G-02, no_std_check.py builds its crate set from the crates that match the attribute, so a crate deleting it stops being checked rather than being reported. The NO_STD_CRATES ratchet F-X009 added is a second mechanism and not a fix, and it is why this one is not urgent. G-04, validate-handoff needs a literal Head field and parses the branch as a bare token, so backticks break it and this repository writes every path in backticks, which cost one handoff rewritten at integration in S03. It is a false positive rather than a fail-open, which is why it is last. Each fix must be observed red before it is claimed, and each closes by making its declared defect probe start passing, at which point the census fails until the declaration is removed in the same change. PART TWO, the refusals the census watches with nothing, and the limits it records instead of covering. The uncovered entry is bench.runner, whose refusals in tools/bench/run.mjs are argument and run-time validation that no suite opens: that entry claimed scripts/tests/test_bench_check.py until the review's second pass measured that the suite never opens the file, and the false claim was replaced by a gap. The recorded limits sit on target-features, packages, split-hld, bench.cold-start, bench.page and panic-probe, SIX and not seven, each blocked on a browser, an npm install, a private source document or a dependency graph a sandbox cannot build. spikes.compare was listed here as a seventh until the S03 review's thirteenth pass and it is not a limit: catalogue.py gives it kind not-a-guard with a reason, so guard_census.py prints it in the out-of-scope bucket and never beside an owner, and it never named F-X010. Run python3 scripts/guard_census.py and count the LIMIT lines carrying this story's id rather than trusting this sentence. All six named owner F-X010 until this pass, and F-X010's recorded scope is CI floor equivalence and the duplicated --sprint and --all arms, which mentions none of these files. A two-week story about a gate profile will not write argument-validation tests for a benchmark runner, so the ownership was as false as the coverage claim it replaced. This story owns them: cover what a sandbox can reach, and for each that a sandbox cannot, either move the limit to a real story or record it with a reason that is not a story id doing no work. python3 scripts/guard_census.py prints the current uncovered entry and every limit with its owner, and the count in ci/guard-probe-budget.json is the ratchet, so closing this story means that number goes down and sweep_complete goes true.

stories.story: Execute the skills' worked examples, because the skills gate asserts nothing about their numbers
stories.notes: bin/ocelli.sh gate skills runs only sync_agent_skills.py --check, which compares a SHA-256 of each skill against its Codex adapter. It detects that a skill CHANGED and asserts nothing whatever about whether a number inside it is right. Nothing in scripts, bin, ci or githooks executes a skill's fenced block or checks a value against a formula. That matters more than it sounds, because .claude/skills/dicom-expert and dicom-tooling are what an agent loads BEFORE writing the LUT chain, so a wrong value there reaches ocelli-pixel by the shortest path there is. Measured in the S03 sprint review: both skills reproduced HLD 18.3's LINEAR_EXACT(-160) = 1.594, which deviation D-13 records as wrong because both functions clamp at -160 and section 18.2's formula gives 0.000, and separately TWO of the eight claimed output numbers in dicom-tooling's own Python block were wrong. All of those had survived every gate this repository runs. They are corrected now and the block is byte-identical to its real output, so a gate arm that ran each python fence and diffed it against the fenced output beneath would pass today and would have caught all three then. The good counter-shape already exists in the same file: the stored_value block carries three asserts and passes when run. This story builds that arm. Note the interaction with F-X009's census, which will want a catalogue entry for whatever new refusal it adds.

stories.story: Try the next adapter when the best candidate cannot open a device, and record what was attempted
stories.notes: probe.rs measure_chosen calls request_device on the single adapter choose_candidate returned and never tries another, while native enumerate_adapters(Backends::all()) commonly returns several. On a host with a broken Vulkan ICD beside a working GL driver the best candidate is the Vulkan A-candidate, request_device fails, and the session resolves tier C with a tier-B path present and unattempted. Tier C renders nothing until F-X001 to F-X004, so the outcome is renders nothing rather than renders on tier B. classify's step 4 was justified by the sentence there is no GPU path to be had, and the S03 review's fourth pass replaced that with what is true, that the best candidate could not open a device and no other adapter was tried. THE COST IS THE EVIDENCE DESIGN AND NOT THE LOOP. TierSignals carries a single device_created bool, so it becomes per-adapter or a list of attempts, classify's step 4 and the NoDevice diagnosis change meaning, the classify_is_total invariant that a GPU tier ALWAYS means a device was created needs restating over the new shape, and the OCELLI_TIER override clamp reads the same field. The story must also decide the fallback order and whether a failed adapter is recorded.

stories.story: Close the measured escapes from the wasm linear memory view ban, which needs type-aware linting
stories.notes: HLD 17.2's rule is that a view over wasm linear memory is built in exactly one place, because the memory moves on growth and a cached view then reads freed bytes with no error. The eslint ban has three selectors and the S03 review's fourth pass measured seven routes past it. Five escape: a function parameter typed WebAssembly.Memory, computed member access such as wasm["memory"].buffer, an assignment alias, a call result, and a class field read through this when the field is RENAMED. The pass 4 reviewer reported four and the remediation measured five, because this.memory.buffer is CAUGHT by the first selector and only a renamed field escapes, so the fifth route is the renamed one rather than the this route. eslint.config.js carries the measured table and is the record. THE FUNCTION PARAMETER ROUTE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS because it is how anyone would write a drain helper, and a module-level cache behind it is HLD 17.2's named failure with one indirection and a green lint. A fourth selector matching any new Array or DataView on a .buffer argument catches all five escapes and therefore all seven and costs exactly one real site, decodeRecord in packages/core/src/errors.ts, which builds a DataView over a caller's own Uint8Array. Accommodating that site with the mechanisms this repository has means adding errors.ts to ALLOWED_TO_DISABLE, which switches every selector off in that file and would make the direct form legal there, so the cheap fix trades a narrow hole for a wide one. Type-aware linting is the real answer and it is a build change rather than a config line, which is why this is a story and not a remediation. THE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF THE TITLE. The pass 4 reviewer measured four escapes, the remediation measured five, and the fifth pass measured three more, a for-of binding, a getter returning wasm.memory, and computed member access on buffer as in new DataView(wasm.memory["buffer"]). A number in the title would have gone stale three times in two passes. THE FOURTH SELECTOR IS NOT SUFFICIENT: it catches the first two of those three and not the computed one, because it keys on arguments.0.property.name equal to buffer and a computed member's property is a Literal with no name. So this story cannot be closed by landing the fourth selector plus an allowance for errors.ts. Type-aware linting remains the answer and the acceptance test is the computed route rather than the function-parameter one.

stories.story: Make close-preflight see the sprint review, and key its verification on the tree it is about
stories.notes: python3 scripts/sprint_workflow.py close-preflight prints OK: S03 is ready to close on a tree that had just taken nine sprint-level review passes and eight remediation commits, the last of which found HLD 17.2's central architectural rule guarded by nothing. THE GREEN IS NOT WRONG, IT IS ABOUT A DIFFERENT QUESTION. cmd_close_preflight reads the last entry of each feature's reviews list, which /complete-feature writes per F-ID at completion. Every S03 row in .claude/scratch/S03-run.json records pass 1 with zero defects, F-X007 records pass 2, and the sprint-level review loop that WORKFLOW.md step 5 describes writes nothing into that structure at all. So the preflight is structurally blind to the review that actually found this sprint's defects, and it says so in the language of success, which is the exact shape AGENTS.md already names about git add -N: the guard answered a question about an empty set. SECOND AND SEPARATELY, sprint_verified accepts any recorded profile=sprint entry with result=pass and the entries carry no tree hash, so a verification taken eight commits ago still satisfies it. The mechanism to fix that already exists and is not used: .claude/verify-ledger.json keys on git write-tree and scripts/verify_ledger.py check-commit asserts the trailer's tree matches the commit's. THE COST IS THE STATE SHAPE AND NOT THE CHECK. S03-run.json has no place to record a sprint-scope review, so the schema gains one, /microscope at sprint scope has to write it, and the preflight then requires the LATEST sprint-level pass to be zero-defect and zero-smell rather than the per-feature ones. The verification half should record the tree hash beside each entry and refuse one whose tree is not the current index, which is the rule CI already applies to the Ocelli-Verify trailer. Note the interaction with F-X009's census, which will want a catalogue entry for the new refusal, and note that .claude/scratch/ is gitignored so nothing here is a tracked-file change. MITIGATION, STATED SO THE STORY IS NOT OVER-SOLD: /close-sprint runs gate --sprint itself and no defect reached main because of this, so the failure is in the evidence rather than in an outcome. That is why it is one week and not a blocker.

stories.story: Decide whether a CI step that is not guaranteed to run counts as CI running the gate
stories.notes: NARROWED TWICE, and what remains is one shape. The fourteenth pass filed this with three shapes where a gate is counted as invoked but is not guaranteed to run. The fifteenth measured six more, three of them TOTAL BYPASSES where bash never executes the runner, and the decision was taken rather than held: a gate counted only at the top level of the body. The sixteenth pass then measured THAT reader as a head test and its replacement as a keyword regex that did not know a reserved word is reserved only in command-word position, so `echo done` matched it and one ordinary line of output turned a correct refusal into a pass. Three readers, three passes, each closing the previous spelling. So the modelling was DELETED. `_refuse_unmodelled_shell` now refuses any `run:` body carrying a shell keyword, a `{` or `(`, a `!`, or a `set`, `shopt`, `exit` or `exec` head, and it names the construct so a maintainer is told which word to remove rather than which gate went missing. It is a whitelist, so the next construct nobody thought of fails CLOSED. WHAT REMAINS, and it is this story's whole scope now: the right-hand side of `&&`. `&&` is a SEPARATOR rather than a compound construct, so `false && GATE` carries nothing the whitelist refuses, exits 0 with the gate never run, and is still counted. It is left open because `invoked_gates`' own docstring documents `cd x && bin/ocelli.sh gate y` as a legitimate invocation, so refusing it contradicts a declared behaviour rather than repairing a reader. The acceptance test is written and asserts the hole is still OPEN: `test_the_right_hand_side_of_and_is_the_remaining_residue` goes red when this story closes, which is the signal to delete it. Note that test was written in the fifteenth pass, LOST when the sixteenth rewrote the class around it, and restored, which is why it now says so in its own docstring.

stories.story: Stop gen_sprint_plan.py's write mode silently overwriting a hand-curated SPRINT_PLAN.md
stories.notes: `python3 scripts/gen_sprint_plan.py` with no argument REWRITES `docs/sprints/SPRINT_PLAN.md` from `allocation.json`, and that file is hand-curated after bootstrap, which its own prose says: 'The generator runs once at bootstrap and after that this file is hand-curated, so nothing rewrites a row when the allocation moves.' The S03 review's fourteenth pass ran it to add one story row and destroyed eight paragraphs of corrections earlier passes had written, including the sentence recording that the parity target is 5.8.2 rather than the HLD's v5.8.9, which does not exist. That sentence IS deviation D-11, so the regeneration silently reinstated a version string this repository exists to correct. Measured: the write mode produced 8 insertions and 20 deletions where the three required edits are 3 insertions and 2 deletions. `--check` passed on the damaged file, because it reads F-IDs, sprints, estimates, goal lines and milestone summary lines and NOT the surrounding prose, so the guard that exists here cannot see the loss it is standing next to. The repair is for the write mode to refuse a file that already exists unless it is explicitly forced, and to arrive with its own probe, because a refusal added to a scanned file without one moves the census count. Note the acceptance test cannot be 'the prose survives', since nothing can assert that generally. It is that the bare invocation refuses.

stories.story: Activate the full-corpus candidate-render gate against Ocelli output
stories.notes: F-012 deliberately lands the candidate-directory, coverage and ledger contract before an Ocelli renderer exists. This follow-up connects every current oracle view to real Ocelli output, makes --require-comparison binding in local verification and pre-push evidence, and preserves D-04's rule that CI validates the submitted tree's local corpus record rather than pretending CI owns the ignored corpus or a GPU.
